requirement: When any unrecoverable fault is detected during autonomous flight, the air vehicle shall enter the predefined safe state within 500 ms by commanding zero thrust on all six rotors, holding the tilt-wing and tilt-tail at their instantaneous commanded angles, and neutralizing aileron and elevator deflection to 0 degrees.

requirement: The geofence monitor shall not command return-to-launch while the aircraft remains inside the approved mission geofence, and it shall notify the ground station when RTL is the nearest contingency maneuver for boundary recovery.

instances.explanation: It is unclear whether 'not' negates only RTL command, the entire while-clause, or both conjuncts in the compound requirement.
'It' could refer to the geofence monitor or to the aircraft whose position triggered the evaluation.
'Ground station' may denote the GCS operator console, the radio link, or the physical shelter housing mission equipment.
'Nearest' has no defined baseline metric—spatial distance, time-to-recover, or energy cost—against which RTL is judged nearest.

nuclear_sentences: The geofence monitor shall not command return-to-launch while the aircraft remains inside the approved mission geofence, and it shall notify the ground station when RTL is the nearest contingency maneuver for boundary recovery.

requirement: The flight-termination subsystem shall deploy the recovery parachute within 50 after receiving an authenticated flight-termination command from the ground control station, and shall report parachute-deployment status to the GCS shortly thereafter.

instances.explanation: The numeric value '50' carries no unit of measure, so the deployment deadline could be 50 ms, 50 s, or another interval.
'Shortly thereafter' gives no bounded latency for status reporting after parachute deployment, so readers may treat anything from tens of milliseconds to several seconds as compliant.

nuclear_sentences: The flight-termination subsystem shall deploy the recovery parachute within 50 after receiving an authenticated flight-termination command from the ground control station.

requirement: As defined for the flight-termination interface in REQ-SYS-044, the cross-subsystem safety monitor shall sample propulsion, navigation, and flight-control health telemetry at 10 Hz and shall archive each sample in non-volatile memory. When any monitored parameter crosses an elevated limit, the monitor shall raise a fault alert to the GCS promptly and may optionally recommend activating flight termination if warranted. The monitor shall maintain cross-subsystem telemetry coverage throughout autonomous flight with availability restored shortly after any detected outage.

instances.explanation: 'Elevated limit' specifies no numeric threshold for the monitored parameters that trigger a fault alert.
'May optionally recommend' leaves the flight-termination recommendation non-mandatory and unverifiable, so an implementation that never recommends termination still satisfies the wording.
'Shortly after any detected outage' gives no bounded recovery time for telemetry coverage restoration.

'Sufficiently low' rotor thrust gives no numeric thrust bound during the entry maneuver, leaving hover-capable residual thrust and near-zero thrust as competing readings.

nuclear_sentences: The safe-state supervisor shall command entry into the predefined safe state within an acceptable interval after an unrecoverable fault is declared.

requirement: During TRANSITION_FWD flight, the control-allocation safety-margin monitor shall detect promptly when virtual moment demand exceeds available actuator authority. When authority is inadequate, the monitor shall command a conservative allocation fallback to the flight control system. The fallback shall keep altitude deviation at acceptable levels within 15 of the commanded transition profile, and anomaly events shall be reported to the safe-state supervisor in a timely manner before transition completes.

instances.explanation: 'Promptly' gives no bounded detection latency when actuator authority is exceeded during transition, so sub-cycle and multi-second detections both remain plausible.
'Inadequate' actuator authority is a subjective judgment with no quantified margin or saturation threshold.
'Conservative allocation fallback' does not specify which actuators, margins, or allocation law the fallback employs.
The value '15' has no unit, so altitude deviation could mean 15 cm per simulation results or 15 m.
'Acceptable levels' of altitude deviation provide no numeric bound tied to the ~15 cm transition performance reference.

requirement: When an operator revises the mission geofence, the geofence calibration module shall not shift boundary vertices by more than 3 without dual-operator approval. When the tower approves reduced-margin operations, the module shall set clearance margin to the tightest feasible value. instances.explanation: Scope of 'not' is unclear whether it forbids any vertex shift, shifts above 3 units, or shifts without approval.
'Tightest feasible' clearance margin has no baseline distance or feasibility criterion, so competing geometric clearances can all be claimed as the tightest feasible value.
'The tower' may refer to the GCS operator role, the mission-control facility, or the datalink authority channel.
'Logged appropriately' is subjective and specifies no log format, retention period, or completeness criterion against which logging quality can be verified.
The offset limit '3' has no unit, so vertex shifts could be bounded in metres, degrees, or grid cells.
